title: Fenwick Tree Range Sum
statement: An array of `n` zeros is updated with a Fenwick tree, also called a binary indexed tree. Each operation is [0, index, delta] to add, or [1, left, right] to query. Indexes are 0-based and ranges are inclusive. Return the result of every query, in order.
hints: A Fenwick tree stores partial sums. Index i in the tree, using 1-based indexes, covers the range ending at i whose length is the lowest set bit of i.
add walks upward by adding the lowest set bit. A prefix sum walks downward by clearing the lowest set bit.
A range sum is prefix(right) - prefix(left - 1). Convert 0-based indexes to 1-based indexes at the boundary.

approaches.name: Plain array
approaches.explanation: Correct and slow when both updates and queries are frequent.

editorial: Store n + 1 slots and ignore index 0. To add at a 1-based index, add the delta and jump forward by index & -index. A prefix sum adds the slot and jumps backward the same way. Subtracting prefix sums answers a range. The point of the structure is that both walks are logarithmic.

examples.explanation: The first query sees 6. The second sees the whole array after the update.
A zero cell, then an update.
